summary: This note is a long Wikipedia-style overview of London, covering its air and rail transport, sport, film and television, global economic and academic standing, history, museums, geography and population, policing, landmarks, and medical research. It highlights Heathrow as the world's busiest airport for international traffic, London's dominance in finance and higher education, and its long historical development. The text ends mid-sentence in the higher education section.
one_line: Wikipedia overview of London covering transport, sport, film, finance, universities, history, museums, population, policing and landmarks.
key_facts: London Heathrow Airport, in Hillingdon, West London, is the busiest airport in the world for international traffic.
In May 2012, Chelsea became the first London club to win the UEFA Champions League.
London's 43 universities form the largest concentration of higher education institutes in Europe.
In 2012, London became the first city to host the modern Summer Olympic Games three times.
The British Museum in Bloomsbury, founded in 1753, was the first of London's museums to be established.
The National Gallery was founded in 1824 to house the British national collection of Western paintings.
Waterloo is Britain's busiest station by number of passengers, with over 184 million people using the interchange station complex each year.
Clapham Junction is the busiest station in Europe by the number of trains passing.
The London Underground is the oldest underground railway network in the world.
London has over 480 overseas banks, more than any other city in the world.
Around 325,000 people were employed in financial services in London until mid-2007.
London has the largest number of billionaires in the world, with 72 residing in the city as of 2014.
London contains four World Heritage Sites, including the Tower of London and Kew Gardens.
The Bow Street Runners were established in 1750 as a professional police force.
The Coalition Government cancelled plans for a third runway and a sixth terminal at Heathrow on 12 May 2010.
